newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia state crude palm oil output seen down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia state crude palm oil output seen down.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned oil palm plantations are expected to see a 20-percent drop in production this year from the forecast 1.8 million tonnes, an agriculture ministry official told Reuters on Friday.
He also said the state-run joint marketing agency KPB would resume signing crude palm oil export contracts in November after a freeze in October because of overselling.
The official said production in state-owned plantations had been affected by the weather, last year's shortage of fertiliser and the advancing age of trees.
"We are expecting a 20-percent decline in production from the 1.8 million tonnes forecast for 1996," he said.
The official also said that the state-run joint marketing agency KPB would resume signing crude palm oil export contracts in November, after a freeze in October.
"The KPB did not sign new contracts in October because it had committed twice the monthly average in September...of about 100,000 tonnes," he said.
The agency, which markets all the crude palm oil produced by state plantations, sells 70 percent of the output locally and exports the rest.
Indonesia's total crude palm oil production has been forecast to increase to 4.9 million tonnes this year from 4.5 million tonnes in 1995.
